learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide students with knowledge about the fundamentals of electrical networks (e.g., functions, voltage/frequency levels, architectures, components, voltage-frequency regulation) and power quality. The level of technical detail is modulated to be consistent with the educational objectives of the Energy Curriculum of the Degree Course in Mechanical Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Overall architecture of the electrical system and its sections (generation, transmission, distribution)
Electrical generation
Transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Network components (conductors, management and maneuvering elements)
Transformer substations
LV lines (sizing and verification criteria)
Overvoltages and related protection components
Overcurrents and related protection components
Elements of electrical safety including strategies and related protection systems/components
Three-phase system power factor correction
Frequency and voltage regulation of networks
Introductory elements to the electrical system
Electrical generation: Hydroelectric, thermoelectric, nuclear power plants and interconnection to the electrical grid
Solar thermodynamic, geothermal, and tidal power plants
Transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Components of electrical transmission and distribution systems: electrical lines
Components of electrical transmission and distribution systems: other components
AAT/AT and AT/MT TRANSFORMER SUBSTATIONS AND MT/BT DISTRIBUTION
Sizing of LV distribution lines
Verification of LV distribution lines
Overvoltages and related protection systems
Overcurrents, protection systems and sizing
Physiological effects of current in electrocution events
Direct and indirect contacts
Earthing systems: functionality, architectures (TT, TN, IT), fault current, touch voltage, coordination of protections
Three-phase system power factor correction
Notes on frequency and voltage regulation of networks
degree: Corso di laurea in Ingegneria meccanica (L-9)
